findings.description: ABEE is retained as REJECTED_LABEL: the primary Cosmo Bio GlyScope brochure explicitly identifies the ethyl ester, not CHEBI30753 free acid. The exact concentration token p-aminobenzoic acid (0.3 μg/μL) is also non-resolving: NBRC1604 explicitly adds10uL of that preparation and TOGO M3052 calls it4-aminobenzoic acid solution. No solvent, complete stock recipe, receiving concentration or transfer to an ester owner is inferred. Preserve the supported Paraamino benzoic acid alias. PMID31986050 remains genuine cocrystal context, qualified PARTIAL rather than exact-owner or role support; other charge aliases and provisional roles remain unapproved.

Promote the variable-n ferric sulfate primary identity to cas:15244-10-7 under MAPPING_SEMANTICS§3: independent Wako product pages explicitly pair that CAS with Fe2(SO4)3·nH2O. Retain CHEBI53438 iron(3+) sulfate as the asymmetric broader grounding (NARROW_MATCH); do not use CHEBI131387 monohydrate as exact, copy anhydrous formula weight, select n, or assert historical lot procurement. The old no-own-CAS rationale is superseded, with its full original preserved in predecessor evidence/history. JCM413→369 and603→592 are available:369 separately autoclaves0.5% variable-ferric-sulfate solution in0.1N H2SO4 (percent basis unspecified);592 includes0.01g variable ferric sulfate in SolutionA alongside distinct ferrous sulfate and ferric citrate. Failed JCM1250 Nothing-found retrieval is not positive source proof; source-specific TOGO evidence is separately bound. The competing UNMAPPED0385 owner and issue873 remain unresolved; no winner or merge is selected.

Use exact active MeSH concept mesh:M0314280 chrome alum, dodecahydrate, supported by NLM narrower-concept/registry context and the supplier KCr(SO4)2·12H2O/CAS7788-99-0 identity. Preserve CAS7788-99-0 as chemical property. This potassium/chromium double sulfate differs from CHEBI53471 Cr2(SO4)3 in potassium and sulfate stoichiometry as well as water; retire the old active hydrate-only CLOSE_MATCH rationale instead of substituting NARROW_MATCH. Full prior evidence and all history remain preserved. The JCM1033 Nothing-found capture is not original recipe proof; use separately inspected TOGO/MediaDive captures at their stated source/version scope. No quantity normalization or whole-owner release is approved.

Retain Na malate, Na-malate and the truncated Sodium Malate And as non-resolving provenance on the exact disodium(S)-malate owner. The generic names do not fix sodium ratio/stereochemistry; source477 database CAS alone is not independent stereo proof where the provider also assigns L identifiers to DL labels. Source1316 explicitly names a20% preparation, independently handled as a stock with unresolved solute stereochemistry. Keep the previously rejected DL tokens and valid explicit L names; do not change the preferred term, identity or select an alternative source form.

Retain Iron ammonium sulfate hydrate and Fe(NH4)2(SO4)2 as non-resolving global provenance on the exact hexahydrate owner. The former is only related in CHEBI76181 and omits oxidation/hydration scope; the bare formula has actual anhydrous and seven-water alternative owners. Preserve the supported source-specific MediaDive106 interpretation because its independent CAS7783-85-9 and six-water formula disambiguate that occurrence. A source-qualified interpretation is not an unconditional resolver synonym. Keep all supported explicit six-water aliases and earlier concentration-label rejections.

Preserve the literal (NH4)2Ni(SO4)2 x 6 H2O (0.1% w/v) as REJECTED_LABEL on the chemical owner: its explicit concentration denotes preparation-qualified scope, not an unconditional neat-salt identity. No solvent, receiving dose or recipe completion is invented. Exact six-water source interpretations remain supported separately. The duplicated bare/explicit nickel owners and conflicting CAS annotations remain held under1050; no anhydrous identity or owner winner is inferred.

Preserve the literal (NH4)2Ni(SO4)2 x 6 H2O (0.1% w/v) as REJECTED_LABEL on the chemical owner: its explicit concentration denotes preparation-qualified scope, not an unconditional neat-salt identity. No solvent, receiving dose or recipe completion is invented. Exact six-water source interpretations remain supported separately. The duplicated bare/explicit nickel owners and conflicting CAS annotations remain held under1050; no anhydrous identity or owner winner is inferred.

Preserve vanadic sulfate pentahydrate as REJECTED_LABEL rather than an exact vanadyl alias: CHEBI132758 classifies this text only as related, and no inspected primary evidence establishes the ambiguous vanadic oxidation nomenclature as unconditional exact V(IV) identity. Keep the explicit vanadyl pentahydrate identity and valid five-water spellings, both CAS annotations/history, and earlier stock/bare-token rejections. This does not select a different oxidation state or source lot.

The exact cobalt(2+) sulfate--water(1/7) label belongs to CHEBI91244 heptahydrate, whose definition/formula explicitly include seven waters. Retain that literal as REJECTED_LABEL on anhydrous CHEBI53470; preserve the prior other heptahydrate rejections and all original source credit. No blanket rejection of generic cobalt names is made.

Retain Cobalt(II) chloride--water (1/7) as REJECTED_LABEL on the exact CHEBI53503 hexahydrate owner. The explicit water ratio1/7 conflicts with the six-water definition, formula and structure. Preserve valid six-water names and the original literal/source/history; this does not infer any source reagent identity from a malformed formula.

Retain MnCl4 x 4 H2O and MnCl4・4H2O as REJECTED_LABEL on manganese(II) chloride tetrahydrate. Both original JCM616 and MediaDiveJ616 preserve the Cl4 text; neither supplies a corrigendum or product identity proving it means Cl2. CHEBI86368 explicitly has two chlorides. Preserve original merge/backfill history and the raw source tokens; the plausible typo is not silently corrected, and case140 remains unresolved pending original author/reagent evidence.

Retain the four existing Feromax, Feroritard, Ferro-Gradumet and Fespan tokens as REJECTED_LABEL, with original credit/history. CHEBI75834 explicitly lists each as a related BRAND NAME; this does not establish that the complete commercial product is identical to neat iron(II) sulfate monohydrate. No product composition or replacement product owner is invented. The supported source1735 monohydrate interpretation and its exact CAS remain unchanged.

Replace only the anhydrous InChI/SMILES inherited via CHEBI53470 with the exact seven-water structures directly reported by CHEBI91244. Preserve the heptahydrate formula and CAS10026-24-1; provenance distinguishes the new structure source from unchanged historical fields. This does not correct malformed source rows or approve receiving concentrations.

Withdraw the fixed-one-water InChI and SMILES from the variable-n vanadyl sulfate owner. CHEBI87020 definition and formula leave n unspecified; the same source contains one-water structures, an internal inconsistency rather than independent support for n=1. Preserve the variable formula, CAS and prior provenance; no replacement fixed structure, hydration count or mass is generated.

Correct the property block at the stated L-disodium malate monohydrate scope using directly retrieved PubChemCID16211643: two sodium ions, one water and explicit S stereochemistry, corroborated by Sigma233935 L-form label/structure. Replace the one-sodium, water-free, stereounspecified CID197014/formula/structures. This is not a CAS reassignment or supplier winner: the same CAS207511-06-6 appears on Aladdin D302750C COA labelled DL, a separately recorded unresolved registry/stereo conflict. Keep the stated owner identity provisionally held, no source-lot equivalence and no resolution of case10 acid-versus-anion ambiguity.

claim_scope: Claim-specific corrections only. Unsupported roles are not classified false; original source/owner release holds remain.
